content.thinking:
I’ve just fixed the map data issue: the viridian map rows are now all the same width, and the validation script confirmed that every map’s grid is rectangular. The next logical step is to start wiring up the UI system, because the core game loop will need a way to present messages, menus, the party screen, bag, shop, and Pokédex to the player. 

Looking at the project structure, I already have a `pokemon.js` module handling species data and a `maps.js` module defining the world. The UI layer is missing; there’s no `ui.js` file yet. I need to create this file and implement a promise‑driven widget stack so that game scripts can `await UI.message(...)` and other async UI calls. 

I recall from earlier design notes that the UI should expose:
- a `busy` flag (true when any widget is active),
- `message` for textbox dialogs,
- `menu` for selectable lists,
- `confirm` as a convenience wrapper,
- `party` for viewing/selecting Pokémon,
- `bag` for inventory,
- `shop` for buying items,
- `pokedex` for browsing the Pokédex,
- `update` and `draw` called each frame,
- plus some helper functions like `wrap` and `drawTextboxFrame`.

All of these need to be defined within a single IIFE attached to `window.UI`. I’ll follow the same pattern used in other modules (e.g., `window.Pkmn = (() => { … })();`). The widget stack will be an array `stack`; the topmost widget gets its `update` called each frame, and all widgets get drawn in order.

I’ll implement `wrap` to split text into lines of up to 36 characters, respecting explicit newline characters. The `message` widget will handle progressive character display, paging, and sticky behavior. It will push itself onto the stack and return a promise that resolves when the message is dismissed. The `menu` widget will calculate its dimensions based on option text widths, handle navigation with up/down, selection with A, and cancellation with B. The `confirm` function will simply show a sticky message and then a Yes/No menu.

For the party screen, I need to draw each Pokémon’s sprite, name, level, HP, status, and a selection rectangle. The bag widget will list inventory entries, handle scrolling, and resolve with the chosen item id or null. The shop widget will be async: it greets the player, shows the player’s money, lets them pick an item, choose a quantity, deduct money, add to the bag, and loop until they cancel. The Pokédex widget will let the player scroll through the 151 entries, display basic info and a sprite for the selected Pokémon.

Finally, `update` should call the `update` method of the topmost widget, and `draw` should iterate over all widgets in the stack and call their `draw` methods. I’ll expose all these functions in the returned object.

All of this can be written directly into a new file `D:\project-5\js\ui.js`. I’ll use a single Write tool call with the full content of the module as the `content` argument. This will create the UI module ready for integration with the main game loop.
